uses.label: Syriac Catholic Church
uses.finding: Celebrant missals 1843 and 1922 remain the documented altar-book states. The auxiliary deacon line is now labelled 1868, 1881, an undated reedition, 1905 (acquired; preface describes a manuscript-corrected text and a new propers part), 1926 and a reported 1931 booklet, with a dated 1868 Mardin manuscript and a Beirut 1888 minister's book beside it. Complementary calendars (1877, 1887), pericope table (1901) and lectionaries (1912, 1925) are labelled. Post-1922 books (Hayek 1978, 1993, 2006; Musa 2003; Mosul 2015) are named from catalogues and community bibliographies only.
uses.limit: No post-1922 celebrant book has been seen, so a reported 1978 order change is unverified; pre-1843 diocesan manuscripts are not enumerated.
next_sources: Patriarchal library and seminary press lists at Sharfeh
Armalet, Catalogue des manuscrits de Charfet (1937)
Coakley and Taylor, Syriac Books Printed at the Dominican Press, Mosul (2009)
The 1978 Hayek order of the Mass and the 2015 Mosul book themselves

uses.label: Syro-Malankara Catholic Church
uses.finding: Pampakuda 1886 and 1931 non-Catholic books are labelled with secondary reception reports; the 1934 two-anaphora book gains a reported institution-narrative change; Catholic-approved Syriac Xystus Taksa printings of 1960 and 1965 were acquired; the 1987 nine-anaphora book is reported; the 2006 synodal approval gives primary-described changes for the Malayalam Takso released in 2007, with a separate Qurbonokramam published by February 2007. Vernacular translations (1966 Malayalam, 2012 and 2023 English, 2020 Kannada, 2022 German, earlier English and German) are labelled as deferred.
uses.limit: The 1934, 1987 and 2007 books themselves are unseen; Catholic reception of the 1886 and 1931 books rests on secondary statements; the Syro-Malankara and Syriac Catholic uses are kept separate except where a manuscript copy from Sharfeh is attested.
next_sources: Malankara Catholic archives at Trivandrum and Tiruvalla; van der Ploeg, The Christians of St. Thomas in South India and their Syriac Manuscripts (1983)
Madey, 'Die liturgischen Bücher der Syro-Malankara-Kirche', OS 22 (1973)

versions.label: Missale syriacum juxta ritum ecclesiae Antiochenae Syrorum, Rome: Propaganda Fide, 1843
versions.distinctness_basis: Retained canonical celebrant missal; seven anaphoras checked by the earlier pass. No new evidence in this lane.
versions.unresolved: Full native-text collation against 1922 remains open (stage gap west-syriac-stages-rome1843-collation).

versions.unresolved: Comparison of the 1881 ordinary with the 1905 Sharfeh book has not been made.

versions.label: Missale iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Apostolicae Antiochenae Syrorum auctoritate recognitum, Sharfeh 1922
versions.distinctness_basis: Retained revised celebrant missal. This pass re-read the reviewer's image of printed p. 13: its footnote cites British Museum Add. 17128 for the older Twelve Apostles commemorations, which supports the new Add. 17128 comparison record.
versions.unresolved: Later Syriac Catholic celebrant books (1978 and after) remain unacquired, so 1922 is not shown as final.

versions.label: Service de la messe privée selon le rite syrien, Mosul 1868 (Ziadé's title; first trial diaconicon)
versions.distinctness_basis: First edition of the Mosul deacon and server book of which 1881 is the 'nouvelle édition'; a distinct printing whose textual difference from 1881 is unproved.
versions.unresolved: No copy located; Coakley and Taylor's Dominican-press bibliography (2009) was not examined.

versions.label: Patriarchally approved undated reedition of the Mosul Service de la messe
versions.distinctness_basis: Named by Ziadé as a further reedition approved by the patriarch; no year, place or textual change is reported, so it stays a reprint witness without chronology.
versions.unresolved: Year, imprint and identity unknown; it might coincide with another listed printing.

versions.label: Borgia Syriac MS 127 (Scher's numbering): Service de la messe selon le rite des Syriens catholiques, edited by Mgr David, written at Mardin in 1868
versions.distinctness_basis: A dated Catholic manuscript of the Mass service, Syriac text with Arabic rubrics, 519 pages; its relation to the Mosul 1868 print is unknown.
versions.unresolved: Present Vatican shelfmark and contents unchecked; whether it is a deacon book or a celebrant book is not stated.

versions.label: Liber ministerii (Syriac title rendered by Brightman as 'the book of the clerks used in the ecclesiastical ministries'), Beirut 1888, Syriac only
versions.distinctness_basis: Listed by Brightman 1896 under the Syrian Uniat books as a separate minister's book; not identifiable with the Mosul line or the 1905 Sharfeh book on present evidence.
versions.unresolved: Book unlocated; a pencil note in the Bonn copy of the 1905 book names a first edition of 1884 (Beirut, Jesuit press, 44 pages), which may or may not be related.

versions.label: Kitāb khidmat al-quddās ḥasab ṭaqs al-kanīsa al-suryāniyya al-anṭākiyya (Šumlājā de-qurābā), collected and arranged by Patriarch Ignatius Ephrem II Rahmani, Sharfeh 1905
versions.distinctness_basis: Ziadé's first complete diaconicon. Its preface describes concrete changes: the deacon's text corrected against old manuscripts, Arabic kept only for the Creed, Trisagion, diptychs, litanies and Lord's Prayer, a new second part with the variable chants of Sundays and feasts, appended Arabic fraction hymns, and a patriarchal order to follow the book.
versions.unresolved: Preface claims are the editor's; no collation with 1881. The 1912 catalogue year is kept as a catalogue role only.
